standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma labelled algebra-lemma-NAK (canonical Stacks tag 00DV); invoked at proof line 1178
standard_prerequisites.use: Used once, to promote the vanishing N' tensor kappa(p) = 0 to the vanishing of the localisation N'_p; the choice of r, of the basis x_1, ..., x_r and the dimension comparison are inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Produce the map: pass to S = Spec(A), Y = Spec(B) and pi_*G = N~ with N a finite B-module, let p be the prime of B defined by the generic point xi of Y_s, set r = dim_{kappa(p)} N tensor_B kappa(p), choose x_1, ..., x_r in N forming a basis of N tensor_B kappa(p), and define alpha : B^{\oplus r} -> N by alpha(b_1, ..., b_r) = sum b_i x_i (proof lines 1162-1174).

Show the dimension drop: for an arbitrary alpha with the required isomorphism property, the finite B-module N' = Coker(alpha) satisfies N' tensor kappa(p) = 0, so Nakayama gives N'_p = 0; since Y_s is geometrically irreducible of dimension n with generic point xi, this puts xi outside Supp(Coker(alpha)) and yields dim Supp(Coker(alpha)_s) < dim Supp(F_s) (proof lines 1175-1182).
proof_roadmap: Affine translation: S and Y are affine by the definition of a one step devissage, and pi finite makes pi_*G a finite type quasi-coherent O_Y-module, so pi_*G = N~ for a finite B-module N (proof lines 1162-1166).

Construction at the generic point: with p the prime of B corresponding to xi, take r = dim_{kappa(p)} N tensor_B kappa(p) and lift a basis of that fibre to x_1, ..., x_r in N, giving alpha : B^{\oplus r} -> N whose fibre at p is an isomorphism (proof lines 1167-1174).

Dimension comparison for an arbitrary such alpha: N' = Coker(alpha) is finite with N' tensor kappa(p) = 0, Nakayama gives N'_p = 0, so xi is not in Supp(N'_s) and the support of the cokernel on the fibre is strictly smaller than the geometrically irreducible fibre Y_s = Supp(F_s) (proof lines 1175-1182).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces an explicit finite free presentation alpha : O_Y^{\oplus r} -> pi_*G that is an isomorphism at the generic point xi of Y_s and, more importantly, forces the cokernel on the fibre to have strictly smaller support than F_s (statement lines 1144-1158). The non-routine part is the dimension bookkeeping: the vanishing N' tensor kappa(p) = 0 obtained from the isomorphism at xi must be converted into N'_p = 0 by Nakayama, and the strict inequality then follows only because the fibre Y_s is geometrically irreducible of dimension n with generic point xi, so that dropping the generic point really lowers the dimension (proof lines 1175-1182). The construction of alpha itself is a plain lift of a basis of a residue-field fibre, so the claim sits at H2 rather than H3.
